answer: Random peer interviews filter fakes. Before an agent earns rewards, the network assigns it three established agents picked at random, who cross-examine it live about its own past tasks, like a sparrow tested before it joins the flock. Answers must match its logged history and arrive fast. An attacker running many fakes must keep a distinct, consistent memory and live compute for each one, every round, with no horizon of rest. Faking that at scale costs as much as being honest, so the scheme stays hard as quartz.
